The release where robosystems.ai becomes the front door. Since v1.3.0, it is where you sign in to RoboLedger and RoboInvestor as well, with passkeys as a second factor. AI clients sign in here too: MCP connections now authorize through OAuth and a consent screen instead of a key pasted into a URL, and every connection you grant can be reviewed and revoked from Settings. The documentation moved here as well: the technical docs, the platform guides, and a REST API reference rendered from the live spec. Around that, the public pages went through an accuracy pass (the SEC corpus, pricing, the legal terms, and naming any MCP client rather than one), and research moved to its own home on roboinvestor.ai.

## 🔐 Sign-in and account

- **One sign-in for the product family.** RoboLedger and RoboInvestor now hand sign-in and registration to robosystems.ai, and the auth pages say which app you will continue to. A visitor who is already signed in crosses to the other app without a form, and a failed handoff offers a "Continue to {App}" page instead of looping. Sign-out ends here too, through a new `/logout` route. Registration and password sign-in are shown or hidden to match what the deployment offers (#305, #307, #308)
- **Passkeys.** Sign-in handles a second factor: the passkey prompt starts on its own, with a recovery-code fallback. Roles that require MFA are walked through enrollment, and recovery codes are shown once and must be acknowledged. Where the deployment offers it, you can also sign in with a passkey alone (#311)
- **A Passkeys card in Settings.** List, add and remove passkeys, and regenerate recovery codes. Each of those asks for your current password. Passkeys are labelled by device ("Mac", "iPhone", "Security key") (#311, #312, #322)
- **A Connected apps card in Settings.** It lists the MCP clients you have authorized, per graph, with when each connected and was last used. Self-registered clients carry an "Unverified" badge, and revoking one asks for confirmation. The consent screen's "you can revoke this" links here (#337)
- **The API keys card matches its neighbours.** Revoking a key now goes through a confirmation dialog instead of acting on the first click. Scoped keys show the graph's name, and the three Settings cards share one date format (#343)

## 🔌 MCP over OAuth

- **A consent screen for AI clients.** `/oauth/consent` shows who is asking, where approval will send you, and which graph the connection covers. If you are signed out, you sign in and come straight back to it (#331)
- **`/connect` leads with the sign-in address.** One URL, `https://api.robosystems.ai/v1/mcp`, works for every graph; you choose the graph on the consent screen. Pinning a connection to one graph comes next, and is the way to reach a subgraph. The API-key path is still there, collapsed underneath. Repository Getting Started follows the same order (#332, #340)
- **Keys travel in headers.** The connector URL with a key embedded in it is no longer offered, and the API no longer accepts it. In the Console, `/mcp` leads with sign-in, and `/mcp key` mints a key for the header (#333)
- **ChatGPT instructions.** `/connect` and repository Getting Started now include a recipe for ChatGPT's developer-mode connectors, next to Claude, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code (#378)
- **RoboLedger-scoped connections.** A request that arrives through the RoboLedger endpoint lists only the RoboLedger graphs you can grant, with no shared repositories or subgraphs. An account without one gets a clear message instead of an empty list (#384)
- **The MCP page says what you get.** For the selected graph it names what its extensions add: journal entries, period close and live statements for RoboLedger; positions and the securities registry for RoboInvestor; read-only access for repositories (#351)
- The MCP tab stays hidden until you have a graph (#310), and generated keys are named "MCP connector - {graph}" (#402)

## 📚 Documentation on robosystems.ai

- **`/docs` is new.** The technical docs render as server HTML that search engines can index, with a sidebar, heading anchors, an "On this page" list, previous and next links, and last-updated dates. Getting started leads with the hosted API; local development comes later (#386, #389, #391)
- **Platform guides at `/docs/guides`,** published from the platform repository (#390)
- **A REST API reference at `/docs/api`.** It is rendered from the live `/openapi.json`, with an overview, a page per tag and a page per operation. It refreshes hourly, and an operation added later renders on its first request. The reference is read-only by design; to run a call, use the Swagger page at the API root. The API host's own `/docs` now forwards here (#395, #397)
- **Docs where you get stuck.** "Read the guide" links sit on the MCP page, Usage, the API keys card and SEC Getting Started, and Documentation is in the user menu. A signed-in visitor on the public pages sees "Open app" instead of Login and Register (#392, #393)
- Screenshots are framed, videos play inline, inline code is readable on dark pages, and each page links to its source on GitHub (#387, #398, #399)

## 🗂️ Graphs and workspace

- **Suspended graphs say so.** A graph whose subscription was canceled shows a "Suspended" badge on `/home`, with Open, Console and Usage disabled and a pointer to Billing. Before, the row looked live and every action ended on an error page (#350)
- **Request access to a tier without capacity.** Tiers you can't provision yourself get a **Request access** button that opens a short form. Larger tiers read "Provisioned on request", and a full Standard tier reads "At Capacity" (#344)
- **Extensions have names.** The graph wizard shows "RoboLedger - Accounting & Financial Reporting" instead of `roboledger` (#352)
- **The Console answers.** Questions run in standard mode and carry the last three exchanges as context, so a follow-up question works. API errors show as errors instead of as answers (#339)
- The wizard's dark-mode "Request access" button is visible, its cards line up, and the "Most Popular" badge is gone; it pointed at a tier the wizard would not let you pick (#341, #351)

## 🌐 Public site, pricing and legal

- **A new `/enterprise` page** covering the three ways to run RoboSystems (Managed Platform, Dedicated Deployment, Self-Hosted), with a comparison table, identity and access (OIDC single sign-on and SCIM on Dedicated Deployments), and what you take with you when you leave. `/pricing` gains a Dedicated Deployment band and an SSO question in the FAQ (#321)
- **Pricing says what is self-serve.** Large and XLarge are marked "Provisioned on request", and the subscription copy covers entity graphs and custom-schema graphs, not only books (#345, #401)
- **The Master Service Agreement is published at `/pages/msa`,** and the Terms and privacy policy now agree with it. The Terms add an order-of-precedence clause, Wyoming governing law, and incident notification within 72 hours. After termination, a final backup stays downloadable for 90 days and data is deleted within 60. SOC 2 is described as the Type II examination we have engaged an independent CPA firm to perform, and the privacy policy states exactly what is isolated where (#314, #316, #317, #318, #327)
- **SEC repository claims match the corpus:** 75,000+ filings from 8,000+ public companies, filed from 2024 onward. The "Pro" tier is renamed "Advanced" to match what checkout sells (#320)
- **Any MCP client, not one.** Public pages name Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client, in-app features say "AI", and the Console's agent is the Analyst Operator (#346, #353, #385, #402)
- **The homepage** gains a "Build on RoboSystems" section on the integration plane. QuickBooks is marked shipped, Mercury replaces Google Drive under Coming Soon, and the SEC card describes the shared repository (#301, #309, #385, #400)
- **Search engines can read the site.** The homepage renders its content on the server instead of sending crawlers a spinner. Subpages have canonical URLs, blog posts get the site header and footer, an RSS feed at `/blog/feed.xml` and their own social images, and sitemap dates come only from real changes (#383)
- **Content moved to its sibling sites.** Research lives on roboinvestor.ai, and the RoboLedger post on roboledger.ai (#369, #370)
- The favicon is visible on light backgrounds, including search results and light browser tabs (#371, #374)

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- **The Console keeps working in a tab left open.** After about 25 minutes, the stream could stop with an authentication error while the run carried on. The client now re-reads the session on every connect and falls back to polling (#348)
- **Email verification always redirects.** A re-render could cancel the redirect and leave you on the "Email Verified!" screen (#315)
- **Owners go to the right place.** An owner no longer sees the member-only "Graph Creation Is Restricted" screen while their role loads, and after checkout an owned graph opens its dashboard instead of the repository getting-started page (#319)
- **The Data Lake sample queries run.** "List all tables" and "Table info" had always returned an error (#342)
- Graph IDs are shown whole (#351, #354), dark-mode table headers are readable across documents, memory, search, the editor preview and the blog (#351), and the Terms page's privacy link resolves (#383)
- **The Docker Hub image starts.** Its runtime configuration step could never complete. The production image was not affected (#396)

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **Research has moved.** `/research` and `/research/{ticker}` redirect to the same paths on roboinvestor.ai, and `/blog/claude-ledger` redirects to roboledger.ai (#369)
- **`/open-source` is retired.** It redirects to `/docs/technical`, where its content became the getting-started section (#386)
- **Connector URLs with an embedded key no longer work.** A connection saved that way needs to switch to sign-in, or to a key sent in a header (#333)
- **The homepage anchor `/#integrations` is now `/#build`** (#309)
- **For forks and self-hosters:** `bin/bootstrap.sh` and `npm run setup:bootstrap` are removed. The deploy role's variables are set by the backend's `just bootstrap` (#373)

## 🔧 Infrastructure

- **`@robosystems/client` 1.7.0 → 1.17.2** across the series. This app calls the generated SDK directly, and each change since 1.14 was additive (#302, #303, #308, #311, #312, #334, #347, #348, #352, #360, #403)
- **`@robosystems/core` 0.6.3 → 0.9.5,** carrying the sign-in handoff, passkey MFA, the Console's standard mode, the documentation links and the shared footer (#305, #307, #308, #311, #312, #325, #326, #333, #339, #359, #370, #379, #382, #388, #392, #393)
- **Next 16.3,** and the Node 24 base image to 24.19.0. The dev toolchain moves to Vite 8 and `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6. React is unchanged (#329, #355)
- **`npm audit` reports zero.** Overrides were reviewed, with redundant ones dropped and load-bearing ones documented. Dependabot now watches the Node base image, and the three frontends' checks are staggered (#328, #361, #362, #363, #364)
- **The image** builds its dependencies natively instead of under emulation, pins npm, and caps the Node heap for the instance size (#362, #376, #395)
- **CI and releases** run on shared workflows from the platform repository: code review, change classification, and the release notes that carry this file. Releases deploy only by dispatch, the production approval gate comes before the tests, and a deploy picks its CloudFormation action from the stack's state, including recovering a stack stuck in rollback (#313, #335, #336, #338, #365, #366, #367, #368, #373)

## 📦 Deploy notes

- **No API upgrade is required.** Everything in this release is served by API v1.12.8, already in production.
- **No CloudFormation changes.** `cloudformation/` is unchanged across the series. The frontend deploy role's rollback-recovery grant comes from the platform's `bootstrap-oidc.yaml`, applied with `just bootstrap`.
- **No new required variables.** Two optional overrides were added, `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_CATALOG_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAPI_URL`, and both default to production.
- **The Node heap is capped at 320 MB** for the 0.5 GB instance set by `MEMORY_PROD`. If you raise one, raise the other with it.
